For a soy sauce substitute in a stir-fry that maintains the savory, umami profile while avoiding soy, coconut aminos are an excellent choice. They offer a similar salty-savory flavor with a slightly sweeter, milder taste and are soy-free. Alternatively, you can use tamari if the allergy is strictly to soy protein but not gluten, though many soy allergies overlap with wheat sensitivities, so coconut aminos are generally safer for strict soy allergies. Another option is a mixture of beef or mushroom broth with a splash of vinegar and a pinch of salt to mimic the depth of flavor.
